doc.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Bringing the Mini Moog and keyboards into Gil Evans' band
summary: With long solos leaving little for a horn player to do, Levin brought a Mini Moog and clavinet with Gil's blessing and gradually shifted from horn to keyboards.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: on the jazz scene going way back: Howard Johnson, Johnny Coles, Jimmy Knepper I think was in the band at that point. I don’t remember whether Dave Sanborn was playing — no that came a little bit later. Lenny White was the drummer at that point and Herb Bushler was playing bass.

I think that was before Lew. It’s really close. Joe Beck played guitar with them somewhere in that period on and off. Joe was having a lot of trouble with his eyes so sometimes he just didn’t want to make club dates. But Billy Harper, Trevor Kohler, it goes on. But there were a lot of really strong soloists. And guys would stand up and take twenty choruses and it would be worth it. It was great. So I’m sitting there as a horn player and this went on for a while. And we’d play a head and then there would be twenty minutes of soloing. And there really wasn’t a whole lot to do. And that had been going on for, I don’t know, a year or so. And I was getting interested in synthesizers and was using them. And I talked to Gil about it. And he said, “Bring one to a gig, try some things.” And I brought it with an amp, it gave me something to do, like in between ensemble sections. And Gil liked it and started writing little pieces for it and I got so I was playing the horn and Mini Moog over here. And then I started to bring a clavinet. Because the guitar players, sometimes he had one, sometimes not, or somebody wouldn’t show up, so I said well I’ll play some chords on the clavinet behind the soloist, and I got the Mini Moog. And eventually I was bringing so much keyboard stuff that it was hard for me to get back to the horn. John Clark joined the band at that point, so we kind of switched and I started playing second horn because John’s great anyway. And I just started focusing on keyboard and then I stopped bringing the horn and that was it.
